name: Cody Whipple
bio: Cody Whipple is a fourth-generation Nevadan from Hiko who runs his family's cattle operation. He built a digital two-way communications network business serving first responders over about 25 years, and played football at Virginia Tech, where he studied animal science. He has not previously held elected office and is the 2026 Republican nominee in Nevada's 4th District.

platform.point: Lower everyday costs for housing, healthcare, groceries and energy.
End federal taxes on tips and defend overtime pay for working families.
Protect Medicaid and Social Security by rooting out waste and fraud.
Supports school choice and career and technical education, with parents in control of their children's schooling.
Vote on Nevadans' needs rather than party leadership instructions.
Backs lower taxes, lighter regulation and more domestic energy production.
Supports H.R. 7008, which would bar members of Congress and spouses from trading individual stocks.
Favors heifer retention programs and origin labeling to prioritize American beef over imports.

economy.evidence: Proposes ending taxes on tips and calls for lower taxes, reduced regulation and a free-market economy.

welfare.evidence: Pledges to protect Medicaid and Social Security while cutting waste and fraud.

liberty.evidence: Guns: pledges to protect Second Amendment rights; LGBTQ: praised a ruling letting states limit women's sports by biological sex.

energy.evidence: General statement backing domestic energy production and reduced regulation.

education.evidence: Campaign site backs school choice and says parents, not government, should control children's education.

notes: Searched the campaign home, issues and news pages and his press releases; web search was unavailable this round, so no local questionnaires were checked. Immigration, security, foreign policy, tech and faith remain unaddressed in his published materials.

name: Nick LaLota
bio: Nick LaLota has represented New York's 1st district in the U.S. House since 2023 and sits on the Appropriations and Small Business committees. A Long Island native and Naval Academy graduate, he served as a Navy officer with three overseas deployments. He later earned an MBA and law degree from Hofstra, served as an Amityville village trustee and worked in Suffolk County government.

platform.point: Cut taxes and restore state and local tax (SALT) deduction relief.
Strengthen border and immigration enforcement.
Support law enforcement.
Pursue peace through strength.
Protect Long Island water quality and secure federal funds for local projects.
Fight fraud, waste and abuse in federal programs.
Honor the service and sacrifice of veterans and first responders.

economy.evidence: Campaign prioritizes tax cuts and SALT relief and contrasts freedom with socialism.

welfare.evidence: Voted yes on H.R. 1, the 2025 One Big Beautiful Bill Act reconciliation bill, in May 2025.

liberty.evidence: LGBTQ: opposes bans on same-sex marriage; abortion: voted yes on the Born-Alive Abortion Survivors Protection Act in 2023.

security.evidence: Voted yes on the Reforming Intelligence and Securing America Act (H.R. 7888), renewing FISA surveillance authority in 2024.

immigration.evidence: Cosponsored the DIGNIDAD Act pairing legal status with tighter enforcement, and voted yes on the Laken Riley Act detention bill in 2025.

foreign.evidence: Voted yes on H.R. 8035, the 2024 Ukraine Security Supplemental Appropriations Act.

energy.evidence: Voted yes on H.R. 1, the 2023 Lower Energy Costs Act expanding domestic fossil fuel production.

tech.evidence: Voted yes on H.R. 7521, requiring divestiture of foreign-adversary-controlled apps such as TikTok, in 2024.

education.evidence: Voted yes on H.R. 5, the Parents Bill of Rights Act, in 2023.

notes: New scores come from House Clerk roll-call records and Wikipedia; the campaign /issues path redirects to the homepage, which lists only issue headings. No record found on religion-in-public-life measures.

name: Chris Gallant
bio: Chris Gallant is a Long Island native who joined the New York Army National Guard at 17 and deployed to Kuwait several times. He has worked as a Federal Aviation Administration air traffic controller, served as a union leader and volunteers as a firefighter. He won the 2026 Democratic primary for New York's 1st District.

platform.point: Use federal investment to bring down Long Island costs for housing, energy and everyday goods.
Oppose cuts or privatization of Medicare, Medicaid and Social Security; add dental, hearing and vision to Medicare.
Let Medicare negotiate drug prices and cap seniors' out-of-pocket prescription costs.
Expand the SALT deduction, the child tax credit and childcare tax breaks.
Fund coastal defenses, flood mitigation, grid hardening and sewer upgrades for Suffolk County.
Protect collective bargaining and require project labor agreements on federally funded infrastructure.
Expand VA care, cut Northport VA wait times and address veteran suicide and homelessness.
Ban individual stock trading by members of Congress and curb dark money in politics.

economy.evidence: Backs action against corporate price gouging, expanded child tax credits and project labor agreements on federal projects.

welfare.evidence: Opposes Medicare, Medicaid and Social Security cuts and proposes adding dental, hearing and vision coverage to Medicare.

energy.evidence: General statement supporting investment in clean energy jobs alongside climate-resilience spending.

notes: Read all six Mission Plan pages, the about page and the media page; none address abortion, guns, immigration, foreign policy, tech, schools or religion. Media coverage describes him as a Black Hawk pilot while the site describes Army National Guard service; the bio uses the Guard description.

name: Jennifer Moore
bio: Jennifer E. Moore is the Republican nominee for New York's 10th congressional district and is described in press coverage as an activist. Education and occupation details have not been widely published.
notes: Checked City & State's candidate page and Wikipedia's NY-10 pages; web search was unavailable this round and no campaign site, social accounts or policy statements were found. All ten topics remain unknown.

name: Michael DeCillis
current_role: Retired police officer and former teacher
bio: Mike DeCillis is the Democratic nominee for New York's 11th congressional district and a fourth-generation Staten Islander. His career includes work as a paramedic and 9/11 responder, ten years as an NYPD officer, civil litigation law, chief of staff in the State Assembly and special education teaching. He ran for this seat in 2018 and 2022.

platform.point: Restore Congress as a co-equal branch and limit governing by executive action.
Cut taxes for working families while making billionaires pay their fair share.
Prevent dismantling of the Education Department and increase public school funding.
Supports a single-payer system without co-pays or deductibles.
Calls for abolishing ICE and for immigration reform that values immigrant workers.
Supports universal background checks, gun licensing and an assault weapons ban.
Supports codifying Roe v. Wade.
Supports the John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act and overturning Citizens United.

economy.evidence: Campaign calls for billionaires to pay a fair share and lower taxes on working families.

welfare.evidence: Advocates a single-payer health system with no co-pays or deductibles.

liberty.evidence: Abortion: backs codifying Roe; LGBTQ: opposes discrimination against LGBTQIA+ people; guns: backs licensing and an assault weapons ban.

security.evidence: Criticizes warrantless ICE searches and arrests and backs reevaluating police response and community trust.

immigration.evidence: Calls for abolishing ICE and opposes racial profiling in enforcement.

energy.evidence: Mostly general statements: calls climate change real and a national security threat, and backs enforcing pollution penalties and green infrastructure jobs.

education.evidence: Opposes dismantling the Education Department and wants more public school investment and smaller classes.

notes: Ballot name is Michael DeCillis; he campaigns as Mike DeCillis. Scores come from his full /issues page; it has no foreign policy, tech or religion positions, and linked S.I. Live articles could not be opened.

name: Manual "Jomo" Williams
bio: Manual "Jomo" Williams is the Republican nominee in New York's 13th congressional district. He has previously run for New York City Council and filed with the FEC as a presidential candidate, and his campaign site describes him as a military veteran.

platform.point: Promotes 'Universal Capitalism' with baseline housing, healthcare, childcare and education as an alternative to socialism.
Replace welfare with guaranteed jobs in infrastructure, public safety and civic work.
Replace NYC sanctuary status with a 'Dignity City' model adding ideological vetting and economic pauses.
Supports the SAVE Act, voter ID and election integrity litigation.
Opposes defunding police and proposes contactless police traffic stops.
Proposes an anti-gentrification law with civil remedies against intentional displacement.
Backs a two-state solution for Israel and the Palestinians with civilian protection.
Expand youth employment programs and community investment.

economy.evidence: Calls for smaller government and lower taxes while also proposing a guaranteed right to employment.

welfare.evidence: Proposes universal baselines for housing, healthcare, childcare and education, funded by redirecting welfare into guaranteed jobs.

liberty.evidence: LGBTQ: supports a two-gender standard and opposes gender-identity lessons in early grades while keeping anti-hate protections.

security.evidence: Opposes defunding police and wants fully funded public safety, while proposing contactless traffic stops.

immigration.evidence: Opposes sanctuary cities and calls for secured borders, ideological vetting and pauses when local unemployment rises.

notes: Read the numbered pages of jmw4congress.com; some listings show him as an independent and the ballot spelling 'Manual' is kept from the input. His two-state stance does not fit the foreign-policy scale, and energy, tech and faith are not addressed.

name: Diamant Hysenaj
bio: Diamant Hysenaj is a construction entrepreneur who founded DCG New York Inc. in 2014 after an earlier firm closed in the 2008 financial crisis. Born in Kosovo, he immigrated to the Bronx at age nine in 1991. He is endorsed by the Republican and Conservative parties in the Bronx and Queens.

platform.point: Draws on his construction background to build more quality housing and create local jobs.
Pairs secure borders with faster citizenship for law-abiding immigrants.
Support small businesses and create jobs in the district.
Lower costs by cutting inefficiency and fraud in the health system.
Make streets safe enough for children to play outside.
Lower taxes for district residents.

economy.evidence: Supports cutting taxes, shrinking government and reducing regulation for businesses.

immigration.evidence: Calls for secure borders combined with faster citizenship for law-abiding immigrants.

notes: Read the campaign home, plan, story and vote pages; they list only short slogans on healthcare, safety and environment, too general to score welfare or security. Web search was unavailable this round, so no local questionnaires or debate coverage were found.

name: Stylo Sapaskis
bio: Stylo A. Sapaskis is a Bronx Republican who was his party's nominee in NY-15 in 2022. He has also run for the New York State Senate in 2010 and New York City Council District 11 in 2025.

platform.point: Criticized inflation and high gas and food prices.
Has backed a $20 minimum wage and more aid for higher education.
Supports ending government funding for abortion providers such as Planned Parenthood.
Supports a larger police presence.

economy.evidence: In voter-guide answers reported by City & State, he backed raising the minimum wage to $20 an hour.

welfare.evidence: In voter-guide answers reported by City & State, he backed more financial aid for higher education.

liberty.evidence: Abortion: supports ending government funding for abortion providers such as Planned Parenthood.

security.evidence: General statement in campaign materials calling for a larger police presence.

notes: Scores rest on his iVoterGuide answers as summarized by City & State, which may date from his 2022 race; the original iVoterGuide page could not be located. No campaign website or social accounts were found.
